title: View controller lifecycle and the responder chain
summary: A view controller goes through load → appear → layout → disappear callbacks; each has a job. Touches find the deepest view under the finger (hit-testing) and unhandled events bubble up the responder chain.
body: **Lifecycle in order:** `loadView` (create the root view; override only when building views in code without a storyboard) → `viewDidLoad` (once: one-time setup, add subviews, constraints) → `viewWillAppear` (every time before showing: refresh data) → `viewIsAppearing` (iOS 13+ back-deployed: sizes and traits are now correct, good for geometry work) → `viewWillLayoutSubviews` / `viewDidLayoutSubviews` (can run many times) → `viewDidAppear` (start animations, analytics, timers) → `viewWillDisappear` / `viewDidDisappear` (stop timers, save, stop observers) → `deinit` (should run when popped; if not, you have a leak).

**Real-life analogy:** A play. `viewDidLoad` = build the stage once. `viewWillAppear` = actors get ready before the curtain opens each night. `viewDidAppear` = the show is running. `viewDidDisappear` = curtain closes; turn off the lights.
**Child view controllers:** `addChild(child)` → add `child.view` → `child.didMove(toParent: self)`. Removing reverses it. Skipping these breaks appearance callbacks and rotation/trait updates.

**Hit-testing:** when you tap, UIKit asks the window "which view is under this point?" and goes down the tree with `hitTest(_:with:)` and `point(inside:with:)`. Hidden views, `alpha < 0.01` or `isUserInteractionEnabled = false` are skipped.

**Responder chain:** if the tapped view does not handle an event, it goes to its `next` responder: superview → view controller → window → application. Used for touches, keyboard shortcuts, menu actions, and "first responder" (the text field currently receiving keyboard input).
keyPoints: viewDidLoad once; viewWillAppear every show; viewIsAppearing/viewDidLayoutSubviews for geometry; viewDidAppear for animations/analytics.
Layout callbacks can run many times - keep them cheap.
Proper child containment: addChild, addSubview, didMove(toParent:).
Hit-testing goes down the view tree; the responder chain goes up.
Check `deinit` to catch leaked view controllers.

mistakes: Reading frame sizes in `viewDidLoad` (not final yet).
Starting work in `viewWillAppear` without stopping it in `viewWillDisappear`, so it runs multiple times.
followups: **Why is my button not receiving taps?** Outside its superview's bounds, user interaction disabled on a parent, or another view on top.
**`setNeedsLayout` vs `layoutIfNeeded`?** setNeedsLayout schedules layout for the next cycle; layoutIfNeeded performs pending layout right now (used inside animations).
**What is first responder?** The object that receives keyboard and edit events first; `becomeFirstResponder()` shows the keyboard for a text field.
